texts: How a holographic sticker is cut, lit and peeled in the browser, with no image files

A die-cut foil sticker with no image behind it: the mark is drawn into a 640 pixel canvas, grown by a 28 pixel disc the way a cutter adds a margin, traced back into outlines with marching squares, and lit by a thin film 120 to 480 nanometres thick. Each step, with the code's own numbers, from the cut to the vertex-shader peel.
